0.text: Most small businesses are invisible to half of Google's searches.

1.text: 46 percent of all Google searches have local intent, according to Google.
That means nearly half of all searches are people looking for something they can find nearby.
If your business is not appearing in those results
you are invisible to half the search market right now.

2.text: 76 percent of people who search locally on a smartphone visit a business within 24 hours
That is a person looking for somewhere to go today.
Local search is not about brand awareness.
It is about customer acquisition on the same day.

3.text: 28 percent of local searches result in a purchase.
One in four people who found you locally will actually buy.
That conversion rate beats most paid advertising channels.
Local SEO is not about vanity metrics.

4.text: This chart shows the priority order for building local SEO from scratch.
Google Business Profile comes first at the top of the impact scale.
Local website signals and citation building are medium impact.
Most small businesses waste time on citations before fixing their GBP and reviews.
Start at the top of this list and work down.

5.text: Your Google Business Profile controls your map listing, your local pack appearance
and the information Google shows when someone searches your business name.
An incomplete or unclaimed profile is the most common reason local businesses do not appear in local results.
Claim it, verify it, and fill in every single field.

6.text: Reviews are the fastest path to local search visibility for most small businesses.
Google uses review count, average rating, and recency as ranking signals.
Businesses with more reviews appear higher in the map pack more consistently than those with strong websites but low review counts.
Ask every customer for a review the same day you complete the job.

7.text: NAP stands for Name, Address, and Phone number.
Every platform where your business appears must show the same exact information.
A phone number written differently on Yelp than on Google creates a data conflict.
That conflict weakens Google's confidence in your location data

8.text: The single most important action for a new small business is claiming and completing your Google Business Profile.
Choose the most accurate primary category.
An incomplete profile is the most common reason a local business does not appear in search results at all.
